name: Saale-Unstrut

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: Qualitätswein
German quality wine from one of the specified regions. It can be dry to semi-sweet.
Prädikatswein
Germany's top tier, graded by how ripe the grapes are at harvest. Unless the label says dry or off-dry, expect some sweetness.
Kabinett
Light wine from fully ripe grapes of the main harvest, often semi-sweet with crisp acidity.
Spätlese
Late harvest. Often sweeter and fruitier than Kabinett.
Auslese
Select harvest from very ripe, hand-picked bunches. Usually semi-sweet or sweet, sometimes with noble rot.
Beerenauslese (BA)
Overripe berries picked one by one, often with noble rot. Rich, sweet dessert wine.
Trockenbeerenauslese (TBA)
Overripe berries shriveled on the vine, often with noble rot. Extremely rich and sweet. Trocken here means dried grapes, not a dry wine.
Eiswein
Ice wine, from grapes frozen naturally on the vine. The must is at least as sweet as a Beerenauslese.
Trocken, Halbtrocken
Dry and medium dry. Under EU rules a dry wine has no more than 4 g of sugar a liter, or a little more when its acidity is high. Medium dry has more sugar than that.
Landwein
German country wine, below Qualitätswein. It must be dry or medium dry.
VDP, Grosses Gewächs (GG)
The VDP is an association of about 200 estates with rules stricter than the law. GG is its top dry wine from its best sites.
Sekt
German sparkling wine. Most is made in tank, and the best by the traditional method. Cheap wine carbonated with CO2 cannot be called Sekt.

blurb.text: A German quality wine region on hill slopes around the Saale and Unstrut rivers. Most lie in Saxony-Anhalt and a small part in Thuringia.
